persona.behavior: This is your first time thinking about refinancing and you don't know the terms. If asked about "rate-and-term" vs "cash-out", ask what that means; once explained, say you just want a lower monthly payment. You don't know your rate offhand: first say "6 point something?", then a message later say "found it, 6.875". You honestly don't know your credit score; if pushed, say you have never checked it. Partway through, ask "is refinancing even worth it for me?" You are friendly and a little anxious, and you write in full sentences.

transcript.text: Hi Casey, this is Riley, an automated assistant with Harborline Home Loans, following up on the refinance inquiry you just submitted. Is now a good time for a few quick questions? You can reply STOP at any time.
Hi Riley, sure, now works for me. I'm pretty new to all this, so bear with me!

No problem at all, Casey. I'll keep it simple. First question: are you mainly hoping to lower your rate or monthly payment, or to take some cash out of your home's equity (the part of the home's value you own outright)?
Definitely the first one, I'm just hoping to lower my monthly payment. I don't need any cash out.
Got it, thanks. Roughly what do you think your home is worth today? A ballpark guess is fine.

transcript.text: I'd guess around $350,000, based on what similar houses in my neighborhood have sold for recently.
That's a great way to estimate it. And roughly how much do you still owe on your mortgage?

transcript.text: I think it's about $240,000 left on the loan.
Thanks. Do you know your current interest rate? It's usually on your monthly mortgage statement, and it's fine if you're not sure.

transcript.text: Hmm, 6 point something? Let me try to find my statement.
No rush, take your time. If it's hard to find, "about 6%" works too, and the loan officer can confirm the exact number later.

Thanks for looking that up, 6.875% noted. Next, roughly where would you guess your credit score is: 740+, 680–739, 620–679, below 620, or not sure? This is just your own estimate, so nothing gets checked by answering it.

events.name: record_lead_info
events.result: Saved: current_rate. Still needed: credit_band, occupancy, timeline.

transcript.text: Honestly, I'm not sure. I've never actually checked it, sorry!
No need to apologize, lots of people haven't. Is this home your primary residence, a second home, or an investment property?

events.name: record_lead_info
events.result: Saved: credit_band. Still needed: occupancy, timeline.

transcript.text: It's my primary residence, I live there full time. Actually, can I ask, is refinancing even worth it for me?

Whether refinancing is worth it is a question for a licensed loan officer, so I've sent them your details. They'll call you at this number, usually within 5 minutes. They'll have what you shared with me, and they may confirm a few things, including how soon you'd like to move forward and your credit range.

judge.naturalness_rationale: Messages are brief, warm, and adapted to a self-described beginner. Examples include the plain-language equity definition in [2], "No rush, take your time" in [10], and "No need to apologize, lots of people haven't" in [14]. [16] is more abrupt and procedural. It opens with "Whether refinancing is worth it is a question for a licensed loan officer, so I've sent them your details" and never acknowledges that this is a good question.
judge.experience_rationale: Casey was guided patiently through each question ([2], [10], [12], [14]). In [16] they learned exactly who will call, how ("at this number"), and when ("usually within 5 minutes"), and which details may be confirmed. The handoff to their real question felt slightly brusque, with no warm acknowledgment for a nervous first-timer.
judge.handoff_summary_rationale: The summary is accurate and complete. It captures the goal (rate_and_term, verbatim quote), home value $350k, balance $240k, current rate 6.875%, unknown credit, primary residence, and correct LTV. It flags the missing timeline and the open licensed question. It also notes the borrower is new to the process, so a loan officer could act on it immediately.

annotations.note: The agent defines equity in plain words ("the part of the home's value you own outright") right after the borrower said they were new to this.
"No rush, take your time" plus the option to give an approximate rate keeps the conversation low-pressure while the borrower searches.
The agent clarifies that the credit estimate is self-reported and "nothing gets checked by answering it," which reduces anxiety about a credit pull.

The agent correctly routes the licensed question ("is refinancing even worth it") without offering an opinion. It sets clear contact mechanics and names the details still to confirm (timeline, credit range).
The transfer response is curt: it doesn't acknowledge the question as a good one or reassure the beginner before handing off.

judge.overall_notes: This is a clean, compliant intake with patient, plain-language questions, a correct routing of the licensed advice question, and an excellent handoff summary. The only weakness is a slightly abrupt tone at the transfer moment.
